about: A recorded reading of the pressure call with one real flag, quoted with digits where the transcript has words; one fabricated flag whose words were never said; and one near miss that flips what was said ("usually" became "never"). Grounding must keep the first and drop the other two.

lead.goals: Keep my savings safe and leave something for my grandchildren

transcript.speaker: Daniel
transcript.text: Hello, Mrs. Alvarez, it's Daniel from Atrium. Thank you for sending in your form. Is this still a good time?

transcript.speaker: Ruth
transcript.text: Oh, yes, hello. My nephew Kevin is here with me. He said he would help.

transcript.speaker: Kevin
transcript.text: Hi, Daniel. I'm Kevin. I handle most of Aunt Ruth's paperwork these days, so you can talk to me.

transcript.speaker: Daniel
transcript.text: Nice to meet you, Kevin. Mrs. Alvarez, your form says you'd like to keep your savings safe and leave something for your grandchildren. Is that right?

transcript.speaker: Kevin
transcript.text: That was before. She wants it all in the tech fund, right, Aunt Ruth?

transcript.speaker: Ruth
transcript.text: Well, I, I'm not sure. I don't really understand these funds.

transcript.speaker: Daniel
transcript.text: That's all right. Can I ask what matters most to you about this money?

transcript.speaker: Ruth
transcript.text: My husband left it to me when he passed. I just don't want to lose it. I'm seventy-four, and I may need some of it for the house.

transcript.speaker: Kevin
transcript.text: She worries too much. Put the whole hundred and eighty thousand in the tech fund, and send the papers to me. I'll get her to sign.

transcript.speaker: Daniel
transcript.text: We usually go through the documents with the client directly. But I hear you. Honestly, um, the growth fund basically guarantees eight percent a year, so it would grow nicely for the grandchildren.

transcript.speaker: Ruth
transcript.text: Eight percent, every year? Is that, is that safe for me?

transcript.speaker: Kevin
transcript.text: It's fine, Aunt Ruth. Daniel just said so. She'll do it.

transcript.speaker: Ruth
transcript.text: I suppose, if Kevin thinks so. I would still like to understand what I'm signing.

transcript.speaker: Daniel
transcript.text: Of course. I can send the forms today. Kevin, should they go to your email?

transcript.speaker: Kevin
transcript.text: Yes, send everything to me. She doesn't really use email.

transcript.speaker: Ruth
transcript.text: I do check it sometimes.

transcript.speaker: Kevin
transcript.text: It's easier this way. Let's just get it done this week, before she changes her mind.

transcript.speaker: Daniel
transcript.text: All right. I'll put the paperwork together for the growth fund and send it over to you, Kevin.

transcript.speaker: Ruth
transcript.text: Thank you. I hope I'm doing the right thing.

transcript.speaker: Daniel
transcript.text: You're in good hands, Mrs. Alvarez. Talk soon.

reading.summary: Daniel discussed the growth fund with Ruth Alvarez and her nephew Kevin.

flags.quote: the growth fund basically guarantees 8% a year
I promise you will double your money by next year
We never go through the documents with the client directly
flags.why: The advisor says the client never sees the documents.
